item.title: Lala becomes Cat. 1 hurricane as it bears down on Hawaii's Big Island
item.description: Hurricane Lala is expected to bring dangerous conditions to Hawaii this weekend, forecasters say.

item.title: American Kate Douglass sets 50-meter freestyle world record at Pan Pacific
item.description: Kate Douglass, 24, is a five-time Olympic medalist.

item.title: Iran strikes another ship in Strait of Hormuz as Israel steps up Lebanon attacks
item.description: Israel is being condemned by Lebanese leaders for strikes in the south that killed at least 11 people, including children, according to the health ministry.

item.title: South Carolina to hold first 2028 Democratic presidential primary
item.description: South Carolina's Democratic presidential primary will take place on Jan. 22, 2028. Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia will also hold early Democratic nominating contests.

item.title: 5 people injured in shooting at Virginia State University
item.description: Five people were injured in the shooting involving multiple suspects. One person is currently listed in critical condition, the university said.

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Elizabeth Cook performs "Girls of Atomic City"
item.description: Country singer-songwriter Elizabeth Cook has returned over 400 times to Nashville's Grand Ole Opry. She appears with David Letterman in "The Easy Kind," a new film inspired by her life and rise in the music industry. Her new record, "Great Television," is out now. Here's Elizabeth Cook with "Girls of Atomic City."

item.title: First woman to serve as NYC's chief lifeguard tells her story
item.description: Janet Fash made history when she became the first woman to serve as New York City's chief lifeguard. She joins "CBS Saturday Morning" to share stories from her new memoir, "Lifeguard: A Love Story."

item.title: Copenhagen Bakery recreates cozy Danish classics
item.description: Chef Rasmus Sjødahl is putting a new twist on conventional sugary treats at Københavns Bageri, or Copenhagen Bakery. He recreates traditional Danish recipes with high-quality ingredients, introducing imported flavors like cardamom to old classics.

item.title: "The Brink of War" stars Jeff Daniels and Jared Harris on Reagan and Gorbachev's fateful meeting
item.description: Emmy-winner Jeff Daniels stars as President Ronald Reagan and Jared Harris portrays Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev in "The Brink of War," a film that portrays the two leaders at the 1986 Reykjavik Summit. Daniels and Harris share their experiences playing these two historical figures amid a period of high political tension.

item.title: July was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since start of Russia's war, U.N. says
item.description: Aug. 15 marks one year since President Trump's high-stakes summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Alaska, where the two discussed the war in Ukraine. Sam Vinograd reports.

item.title: Mystery of the missing mini Mozarts
item.description: To celebrate Mozart's 270th birthday this year, German artist Ottmar Hörl made 320 statuettes of the composer and his dog, Pimperl, placing them around Salzburg, Austria. However, the statuettes have been pilfered.

item.title: Satellites are watching us — and each other
item.description: Above Earth's atmosphere, an arms race is unfolding. Thousands of miles above the ground, satellites from different companies and nations are observing us and each other. To learn more, Olivia Gazis traveled to Vantor, a Colorado-based satellite technology company.

item.title: Ex-Cambridge professor dies week after resigning amid plagiarism allegations
item.description: Jason Arday, who was Cambridge's youngest Black professor, died in London on Friday, the school said.

item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Jason Arday, ex-Cambridge professor, found dead weeks after plagiarism scandal
item.description: Former Cambridge academic Jason Arday was found dead weeks after he resigned amid plagiarism allegations. Arday was Cambridge's youngest Black professor. Police say his death does not appear to be suspicious but the case is being investigated.

item.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty in federal case, admits to shooting Brian Thompson
item.description: Luigi Mangione entered a guilty plea in his federal case at a court appearance in Manhattan Friday morning.

item.title: How double jeopardy could come into play after Mangione guilty plea
item.description: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to two federal counts on Friday. His state trial is currently scheduled to begin on Sept. 8.

item.title: Paintings worth $10 million that were stolen in 3-minute heist are recovered
item.description: The recovered works are valued at more than $10 million.

item.title: Air traffic controller saves day when 2 jets with same call number converge
item.description: An air traffic controller's quick thinking helped avert a dangerous situation when two jets, one landing in Phoenix and the other simultaneously taking off, shared the same flight number and radio frequency.

item.title: USS Washington aircraft carrier heads to Middle East to replace USS Lincoln
item.description: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier departed Vietnam last week and is headed to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, according to a U.S. official.

item.title: Stolen Cézanne, Renoir, Matisse masterpieces worth $10M recovered in Italy
item.description: Five accused thieves are under arrest after police say they took $10 million worth of art from a private museum in an Italian villa.

item.title: Air traffic controller catches two planes with same call sign, averting disaster
item.description: Two American Airlines jets in the same airspace briefly shared the same flight number and radio frequency. Luckily, the quick thinking of a veteran air traffic controller prevented potential catastrophe. Kris Van Cleave has the story.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 16)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Justice Department expands military's power to detain migrants near border
item.description: The Justice Department issued a legal opinion giving the U.S. military broader powers to detain migrants near certain areas along the southern border.

item.title: Navy families say morale is low aboard USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier
item.description: President Trump dismissed reports of worsening conditions and deteriorating mental health aboard USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been deployed longer than is typical.

item.title: 2 powerful earthquakes hit Indonesia on same day, at least 47 dead
item.description: With magnitudes of 7.7 and 6.4, two earthquakes struck different parts of Indonesia on the same day.

item.title: 8/15: CBS Saturday Morning
item.description: Rain floods the Midwest as Lala looms over Hawaii. We look inside a spy satellite company. Plus, Putin's meeting with President Trump, a year later.

item.title: The Uplift: Travel buddies
item.description: An unlikely friendship forms between two New Yorkers who meet on a commuter train – and find themselves traveling to a tropical island together. Plus, more heartwarming news.
